title: In Judges 1 What Does The Inquiry Of The Israelites Reveal About Their Relationship With God After Joshuas Death
paragraphs: Israel’s Inquiry in Judges 1: A Window into Post-Joshua Faith

The opening chapter of Judges provides a fascinating glimpse into the spiritual life of Israel after the death of Joshua. The nation stands at a crossroads, lacking a central human leader. Their inquiry to God about who should lead the continued conquest of Canaan reveals important truths about their relationship with the Lord in this transitional period.
1. Seeking God’s Guidance: A Positive Start
Judges begins with a demonstration of dependence on God. The Israelites, facing uncertainty, turn to the Lord:
And it came to pass after the death of Joshua, that the children of Israel asked of Jehovah, saying, Who shall go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them? - Judges 1:1 ASV

This inquiry indicates a lasting, though fragile, commitment to seek God’s will—a practice modeled by Moses (Exodus 33:13 ASV) and Joshua (Joshua 7:6 ASV). It reflects an acknowledgment that victory and direction come from God, not merely from human strength or strategy (Psalm 20:7 ASV).
2. God’s Response: Assurance and Clarity
God answers their request:
And Jehovah said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand. - Judges 1:2 ASV
This direct reply shows that God remains present and willing to guide His people. The Lord’s answer reaffirms His sovereignty and faithfulness to His promises (Genesis 49:8-10 ASV; Joshua 1:5 ASV).
3. Early Signs of Weakness: Partial Obedience

While the Israelites’ inquiry is commendable, the rest of the chapter reveals growing spiritual compromise. Instead of obeying God’s commands to fully drive out the inhabitants, several tribes fail to do so (Judges 1:21, 27-36 ASV). This partial obedience demonstrates a weakening of faith and trust:
And Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean and its towns... - Judges 1:27 ASV
Their initial inquiry suggests reliance on God, but their subsequent actions reveal inconsistency—a pattern that will repeat throughout Judges (Judges 2:2 ASV).
4. Relationship Reflected: Trust with Growing Distance
In summary, the inquiry in Judges 1:1 reveals:
A continuing awareness of their need for God’s guidance, rooted in the faith of previous generations.
God’s faithfulness to respond, underscoring His desire for relationship and leadership over His people.
A spiritual drift—though they ask for direction, their obedience falters, foreshadowing the cycle of sin and deliverance characteristic of Judges (Judges 2:11 ASV).
This passage challenges believers today to not only seek God’s will but to follow it fully, remembering that genuine faith is expressed in both inquiry and obedience (James 1:22 ASV).
Key Takeaways:
God desires His people to seek Him, especially in times of transition or uncertainty.
Initial dependence on God can fade if not accompanied by ongoing, wholehearted obedience.
Christ is our ultimate leader—He alone empowers us to walk faithfully (Hebrews 12:2 ASV).
